title: poly.toml
description: The poly.toml configuration document for poly's lint, format, hooks and commit surfaces.

exclude_mode.description:
`"replace"` makes `[discovery] exclude` replace inherited globs instead
of accumulating them; any other value accumulates.

lint.description: Per-language linter configuration, keyed by language id then engine name.

fmt.description: Per-language formatter configuration, keyed by language id then engine name.

Extends.description: Base configs to inherit from (ADR 0020): a local path or a pinned remote git file, as a single entry or an array.

oneOf.description: A local path to a base config.
A local path to a base config.

ExtendsSource.description:
One local or pinned-remote base config that a `poly.toml` `extends`.

Field vocabulary mirrors [`crate::HookSource`] for consistency: exactly one of
`path` (local, mutually exclusive with `git`) or `git` (repository URL) must
be set; a `git` source requires a nonempty `revision`; a `path` source must
not set `revision`.

id.description: Optional stable identifier used in diagnostics and the config lock file.

path.description: Local base path (a file, or a directory joined with `file`); XOR `git`.

revision.description: Pinned git revision; required (and nonempty) for a `git` source.

file.description:
Path to the config file within the repository/directory. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BASE_FILE`] (`poly.toml`).

RawDefaults.description:
On-disk representation of `[defaults]`. `line_ending` is a string so the TOML
stays human-friendly; it is normalized into [`LineEnding`] on load.

line_length.description: Target maximum line length, applied wherever a tool exposes the setting.

final_newline.description: Whether to enforce a single trailing newline.

trim_trailing_whitespace.description: Whether to strip trailing whitespace on each line.

DiscoveryConfig.description:
`[discovery]` — tunes the file walk that direct `poly lint` / `poly fmt` /
`poly cache` runs (the CI / GitHub Action path).

The hooks path already excludes per-builtin; this gives the direct-CLI path
the same reach. Globs are gitignore-style and compose with `.gitignore` and
the built-in vendored/generated prune set — they never override an explicitly
passed path argument.

exclude.description:
Gitignore-style globs excluded from discovery. Accepts a single string or
an array (`exclude = "test_apps/**"` or `exclude = ["a/**", "b/**"]`),
matching the `files`/`exclude` shape used throughout `[hooks]`/`[tools]`.

**The matching rule, in one sentence:** a glob that does not begin with
`/` matches a file or directory of that name at *any* depth below the
directory holding this config, while a leading `/` anchors it to that
directory.

This is gitignore's rule, and it is the one thing about `exclude` worth
reading twice, because the unanchored form is what people write by
default:

```toml
[discovery]
# Prunes the top-level e2e/ AND src/test/java/io/xberg/e2e/, because
# `e2e` is also an ordinary Java/Kotlin package name.
exclude = ["e2e/**"]

# Prunes only the top-level e2e/ directory.
exclude = ["/e2e/**"]
```

Nothing warns you when the unanchored form over-reaches — the extra files
are simply never discovered, and the run reports a clean pass over what is
left. `poly doctor` reports any rule that is pruning directories at more
than one depth, which is the symptom.

force_exclude.description:
Apply `exclude` to explicitly named roots too, not just to the walk.

**Defaults to `true`**: a file or directory named on the command line
honors `exclude`, which is what a hook — always handed explicit staged
paths — needs for a repo's excludes to hold. Set it to `false` to restore
the older "an explicitly named path is always checked" behavior for every
run, rather than reaching for `--include-excluded` each time.

```toml
[discovery]
exclude = ["vendor/**"]
# `poly fmt vendor/x.py` checks the file; `poly fmt .` still skips it.
force_exclude = false
```

This governs only *explicitly named roots*; the directory walk applies
`exclude` either way. The CLI's `--force-exclude` / `--include-excluded`
flags override this key in either direction for a single run.

Because the default is `true`, this field is the resolved value, not a
tri-state: "unset" and "set to `true`" are deliberately the same thing,
and the *flags* — not this key — carry the explicit-override signal.

Like `no_prune`, and unlike `exclude`, this is read from the run's **root**
config only: the decision is made once per run, before any path is matched
to the nested config governing it, so a `poly.toml` in a subdirectory
cannot set it for its own subtree.

no_prune.description:
Directory *names* to keep despite the built-in vendored/generated prune
set — the opt-out for a repo where one of those names is ordinary source.

`build` and `dist` are build-output conventions in most ecosystems and
ordinary domain nouns in some (`commands/build/`, a Rust module named
`build`), so the built-in set cannot be right for everyone:

```toml
[discovery]
no_prune = ["build", "dist"]
```

These are bare directory names matched at any depth, not globs — the
built-in set is a name list, and this subtracts from it. To prune *more*
names, use `exclude`, which already does that.

Unlike `exclude`, this replaces rather than accumulates across config
layers, matching every other array in `poly.toml`. It is read from the
run's root config only: a `poly.toml` *inside* a pruned directory cannot
un-prune it, because the directory holding it was never walked.

generated.description:
Whether poly acts on machine-generated files — those whose opening lines
carry a `DO NOT EDIT` / `@generated` / `Code generated …` banner, or a
`<project>:hash:<digest>` content stamp.

**Defaults to `true`**: a generated file is linted and formatted like any
other, which is how a generator bug gets noticed. Set it to `false` for a
repository whose generated output is not its to fix, and whose findings
there are therefore noise:

```toml
[discovery]
generated = false
```

One key for both phases on purpose. "Is this file mine to check?" has a
single answer per file, and splitting it into `[lint]` and `[fmt]` halves
would be two keys a reader must keep in agreement to get the behaviour
they asked for.

Those files are then reported as **skipped**, never silently dropped: the
skip feeds the `checked` count, the JSON `skipped` payload, and
`--deny-skips` / `--max-skips`, so a gate cannot quietly stop covering
them.

Unlike `exclude`, this cannot prune the walk — a banner is content, so
the file must be read before the question can be answered. It is a skip,
not an exclusion, and the resolved value is per-config: a nested
`poly.toml` (ADR 0018) may set it for its own subtree.

This governs whether poly *acts on* the file at all. Whether a generated
file poly did act on may be **rewritten** is a separate, narrower
question that only a content-hash stamp can answer `no` to — see
`--fix-generated`.

Patterns.description: A single glob string, or an array of glob strings.

FreeTable.description: A table of per-language, per-engine configuration keys (`[lint.<lang>.<engine>]` / `[fmt.<lang>.<engine>]`).

preset.description: Named preset to seed the rules from (e.g. `"conventional"`).

write.description: Whether the cleaner rewrites the commit message in place.

message.description: Require the subject to match a pattern.

excludes.description: Subjects matching any of these patterns skip linting (e.g. `^WIP`).

cleanup.description: Find/replace cleanups applied to the message body.

exit_nonzero_on_rewrite.description: Exit non-zero when the cleaner rewrote the message.

title_prefix_separator.description: Separator between the title prefix and the subject.

title_suffix_separator.description: Separator between the subject and the title suffix.

pattern.description: Regular expression the subject must match.

description.description: Human-readable description shown when the rule fails.

pattern.description: Regular expression; matching subjects skip linting.

HooksConfig.description: Git-hook configuration: the reserved keys below, plus one key per git stage (`[hooks.pre-commit]`, `[hooks.commit-msg]`, …).

sources.description: Local or pinned-Git hook producer catalogs.

stages.description: Default stages applied to builtin hooks that do not set their own.

env.description: Environment variables merged into every job.

isolate.description: Whether hooks run against the staged-content snapshot instead of the live worktree (ADR 0019). Unset uses the per-invocation default.

StageConfig.description:
Configuration for a single git stage (`[hooks.pre-commit]`, etc.).

Jobs come from three places, run in this order within the stage:
the ordered `jobs` array-of-tables, then the named `commands` map, then the
named `scripts` map. For a map entry the key supplies the job `name` when
the job omits its own.

piped.description: Run jobs sequentially, aborting on the first failure (lefthook "piped").

follow.description: Stream job output as it is produced.

exclude_tags.description: Tags whose jobs are excluded from this stage.

skip.description: Skip guard — when active, the whole stage is skipped.

only.description: Only guard — the stage runs *only* when active.

fail_on_changes.description: Fail the stage if its jobs dirty the working tree.

precondition.description:
Guard command: exit 0 runs the stage, non-zero (or missing tool) **skips
it with a warning** rather than aborting.

before.description:
Command(s) run after `precondition` passes and before the jobs;
failure aborts the stage. Run sequentially.

after.description: Command(s) run after the stage's jobs succeed; non-zero aborts.

Guard.description: A bare boolean (unconditional), or a list of guard conditions.

GuardCondition.description:
One entry in a [`Guard::Conditions`] list.

Pragmatic subset of lefthook's model: either a bare git-operation name
(`"merge"`, `"rebase"`) / branch name, or a `{ ref = "...", run = "..." }`
match table.

anyOf.description: A git operation or branch name (e.g. `"merge"`, `"rebase"`).

GuardMatch.description: A `{ ref = "...", run = "..." }` guard match table.

ref.description: Branch-ref glob the guard applies to (lefthook `ref`).

run.description: Shell command whose exit status decides the guard (lefthook `run`).

Job.description:
One runnable unit within a stage (lefthook "command" or "script").

A job runs exactly one of `run` (a shell command) **xor** `script` (a script
file interpreted by `runner`); [`super::HooksConfig::validate`] enforces this.

name.description:
Display name; defaults to the map key when defined under
`[hooks.<stage>.commands.<name>]` / `.scripts.<name>`.

run.description: Shell command to run. Mutually exclusive with `script`.

script.description: Script file to run. Mutually exclusive with `run`; requires `runner`.

args.description: Extra arguments appended to the invocation.

glob.description: Glob(s) selecting which changed files this job receives.

root.description: Run the job from this subdirectory.

skip.description: Skip guard — when active, the job does not run.

only.description: Only guard — the job runs *only* when active.

precondition.description:
Applicability probe for this job alone: exit 0 runs it, non-zero reports
it **skipped** (visible, not a failure) while its siblings run normally.

Prefer this to the stage-wide `[hooks.<stage>] precondition` whenever the
prerequisite belongs to one tool — a stage-wide guard withholds every
check in the stage. It is evaluated in the tree the job itself runs in,
which under staged isolation is the staged snapshot, not the worktree.

before.description:
Setup command(s) for this job alone, run sequentially before it.

A failure marks **this job** as having an unknown verdict and fails the
stage, without preventing sibling jobs from reporting theirs. Same tree
as `precondition`.

env.description: Per-job environment variables (merged over the global `[hooks].env`).

fail_text.description: Message printed when the job fails.

timeout.description:
How long this job may run before poly kills it and reports it as timed
out (rather than as having failed on its own merits).

Accepts whole seconds (`timeout = 90`), a suffixed duration
(`"500ms"`, `"30s"`, `"10m"`, `"1h"`), or `0` / `"off"` / `"none"` to run
the job unbounded. Unset means the shape-derived default: a long budget
for a per-file job, a far longer one for a `workspace` job.

Held as raw text and resolved during lowering, where the job's name is
known and a malformed value can name it. The environment overrides
(`POLY_HOOK_TIMEOUT` / `POLY_HOOK_WORKSPACE_TIMEOUT`) outrank this key —
see the `poly-hooks` `timeout` module for the full precedence chain.

priority.description: Lower values run first within a stage (default `0`).

serial.description:
Mutual-exclusion set this job belongs to.

Hooks in a stage run concurrently; `serial` is the opt-out for a job that
cannot tolerate a *peer* running at the same time — a tool holding a
global lock, or two jobs writing the same output. It does **not** stop
the run: a serial job still runs alongside every hook outside its set.

- `serial = true` — join the shared set (never concurrent with another
  `serial = true` job).
- `serial = "cargo"` — join a **named** set; only members of that name
  exclude each other. `"cargo"` is the set the built-in cargo group uses,
  so a job invoking cargo should name it (see [`crate::CargoHooks`]).
- `serial = false` — explicitly concurrent, overriding a stage-level
  `parallel = false` and the automatic cargo grouping.

Unset lets the stage decide: `piped`/`parallel = false` serialize a
per-file job, a `run` line invoking cargo joins the `"cargo"` set, and a
`workspace = true` job otherwise runs concurrently.

stage_fixed.description:
When the job modifies files and exits 0, the runner `git add`s the
matched files and continues; only a non-zero exit fails the stage.

workspace.description:
Whole-workspace job: it compiles or analyses the entire project (e.g.
`cargo clippy`, a type checker like `pyrefly`) rather than a per-file
set. Default `false` (per-file).

This decides whether the job receives filenames, **not** which tree it
runs in: under staged isolation every job — per-file included — runs
against the non-destructive snapshot of the staged index and so never
sees unstaged worktree edits or untracked files (ADR 0019).

interactive.description: The job needs an interactive terminal.

use_stdin.description: Feed matched file contents to the job on stdin.

Timeout.description: Whole seconds (`90`), a duration string (`"500ms"`, `"30s"`, `"10m"`, `"1h"`), or `0` / `"off"` / `"none"` to run unbounded.

Serial.description: `true` joins the shared exclusion set, `false` forces concurrency, and a string joins a named set (`"cargo"`).

JobCache.description:
Per-job result-cache declaration.

`mode` reuses the crate-wide [`HookCacheMode`]; `inputs` lists glob sets the
command depends on; `compiler` opts the job into tier-2 sccache env
injection.

mode.description: Override the cache mode for this job; `None` inherits `[cache.results]`.

inputs.description:
Glob sets the command's output depends on (e.g.
`["**/*.rs", "Cargo.toml", "rust-toolchain.toml"]`).

compiler.description: Opt into tier-2 sccache env injection (`RUSTC_WRAPPER`, …).

HookCacheMode.description:
Controls when hook results are served from the result cache.

The default is [`Safe`] — hook results are cached only when the hook
explicitly declares its inputs via `cache = { inputs = [...] }` in the
job definition.

[`Safe`]: HookCacheMode::Safe

oneOf.description:
Cache hook results only when the hook declares its inputs (default).

Builtins (`lint`/`fmt`) are always cached by matched files
because their footprint equals their input set.  An inline command is
cached only when it carries a `cache = { inputs = [...] }` declaration;
otherwise it always reruns.

Cache based on matched files only, regardless of declared inputs.

May produce stale results for commands whose behaviour depends on
inputs outside the matched file set (e.g. environment variables,
generated files).  **Use with care.**

cargo.description:
The whole-workspace Cargo tool group (`cargo`).

`None` when the `cargo` key is absent — distinct from an explicit
`cargo = false`. With a `[hooks]` section present, an absent key means
the group runs by default (capability-probed); an explicit value wins.

BuiltinHook.description: `true`/`false`, or a table. A table without `enabled` is enabled.

stages.description: Stages this hook runs in; empty inherits the `[hooks] stages` default.

exclude.description: File include/exclude glob(s) for this hook.

FileSafetyHooks.description: `true`/`false`, or a table tuning the file-safety checks. A table without `enabled` is enabled; each member check defaults on.

max_added_file_kb.description: Size ceiling, in kibibytes, for the large-file check.

CargoHooks.description: `true`/`false`, or a table tuning the whole-workspace Cargo tools. A table without `enabled` is enabled; each member tool defaults on.

HookSource.description: One local or pinned Git hook catalog.

id.description: Stable source identifier used in the lock file and cache path.

path.description: Local catalog directory, mutually exclusive with `git`.

git.description: Git repository URL, mutually exclusive with `path`.

revision.description: Git ref resolved by `poly hooks update`.

hooks.description: Explicit producer hook identifiers to enable.

CacheConfig.description:
Configuration for the `[cache]` table in `poly.toml`.

All fields default so `[cache]` is entirely optional.

enabled.description:
Master enable/disable switch for both cache tiers (default `true`).

Equivalent to `--no-cache` on the CLI.

dir.description:
Override the cache root directory.

When absent the cache lives in the per-user cache home (see
`poly_cache::root_from`): `<platform-cache>/poly/<repo-key>`, keyed by the
nearest `.git` / `poly.toml` ancestor.

ResultsCacheConfig.description: Configuration for the tier-1 result cache.

SccacheConfig.description:
Configuration for the tier-2 sccache integration (opt-in, off by default).

When enabled, `poly hooks` starts the shared sccache server (idempotent,
long-lived) before running hooks, and injects `RUSTC_WRAPPER` /
`SCCACHE_DIR` / `SCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE` only into hooks that declare
`cache.compiler = true`.

Sccache is **not implemented in this crate** — this is only the config
surface.  Wire-up happens in `crates/poly-hooks` (Workstream B/C).

bin.description: Path to the `sccache` binary.  When absent, `$PATH` is searched.

max_size.description: Maximum cache size string understood by sccache (e.g. `"10G"`).

ToolsConfig.description:
`[tools]` — a map from catalog tool name to its [`ToolConfig`].

Deserializes transparently from the `[tools.<name>]` tables. Empty by
default (no tools enabled).

ToolConfig.description: Configuration for a single catalog tool under `[tools.<name>]`.

enabled.description:
Whether this tool is active. **Off by default** — declaring the table
is not enough; `enabled = true` is required.

command.description:
Which catalog command to invoke (`""` is the tool's default command,
`"format"`, `"check"`, …). `None` lets poly pick by intent.

args.description:
When present, **replaces** the catalog command's argument vector
entirely; when `None`, the catalog command's own argv is used.

stages.description: Git stages this tool runs in; empty means it is not bound to a stage.

files.description: File include glob(s); `None` matches every candidate file.

exclude.description: File exclude glob(s) filtered from the matched set before the tool runs.

env.description:
Environment variables injected on top of the inherited environment when
the tool runs. Applied on both the direct-engine path and the hooks-lowering
path.

root.description:
Working directory the tool runs in, relative to the config/repo root.
`None` means the repo root. Applied on both the direct-engine path and the
hooks-lowering path.

Stage.description: A git hook stage. The legacy aliases `commit`, `push` and `merge-commit` are also accepted where a stage is named.

WorkspaceConfig.description:
`[workspace]` — marks a config as the cascade boundary for hierarchical
resolution (ADR 0018).

In a monorepo, `poly` resolves the config for a file by deep-merging the
chain of `poly.toml` files from the nearest one up to the workspace root.
Setting `root = true` stops that upward walk at this config, so a project
never inherits configuration from a `poly.toml` above its own root (e.g. one
in `$HOME`). A directory containing `.git` is treated as an implicit boundary
even without this marker.

root.description:
When `true`, upward cascade resolution stops here — this config is the
base of the merge chain.

RulesConfig.description:
`[rules]` — user-defined ast-grep YAML custom-rule directories.

Directories listed here are scanned for `*.yml` / `*.yaml` rule files on
every lint run. Paths are interpreted relative to the config file's directory.
The default is `[".poly/rules"]`; set to an empty array `dirs = []` to
disable custom rules entirely.

dirs.description:
Directories (relative to the config file) containing custom ast-grep
YAML rule files. Defaults to `[".poly/rules"]`.

builtin.description:
Whether poly's built-in ast-grep rule pack (curated, per-language lint
rules embedded in the binary — no `dirs` setup required) is loaded.
Defaults to `true`; set to `false` to lint with only the rules under
`dirs`. The pack is layered *beneath* `dirs`: a user rule with the same
`id` as a pack rule replaces it.
